description:
DONE (2026-09-02): both stages landed on wt/kdt13-boundaries --
fz-kdt.127.1 (8c3d5ce90, stage B: the callable axis names the
construction; CallableShapes, containment admission, PerPosition,
construction-keyed capture unpack) and fz-kdt.127.2 (29b07acfa, stage A:
the forwarder key erases the brand and keeps capture types). samelambda3
prints 12 / 11.0 on interp, JIT and AOT in both call orders with ZERO
dispatch nodes; the dynamic twin (closure chosen at runtime) is correct
with one construction-shape question; the union-capture containment
witness is correct and goes wrong under an overlap swap.

THE DEFECT (as finally understood). A closure value's word already named
its construction wrapper (one per producer position, CallableId =
(function, capture types)) on both doors -- the mint was exact. Every
READER collapsed it to the lambda's FnId: the predicate projection erased
captures, the native identity test admitted every wrapper of the
function, the interp resolver dropped the callable, and the capture
unpack asked all wrappers of the function for one repr. So `closure[L]
(int)` and `closure[L](float)` were one question, the forwarder's
callsite had no test node, the first arm took both, and an int ran
through a float body (interp: 12.0 via a lenient Int-under-F64 marshal;
native: refusal). And the program was STATIC -- every caller knew which
closure it passed; the runtime question was manufactured by the fz-6gb
forwarder erasure dropping capture types along with the brand.

THE PRINCIPLE (user review): runtime tests are the last resort. Static
knowledge flows by KEY; dynamic knowledge flows by the WORD the mint
stamped. No test re-derives what a key or the word already says.

ORDER, proven by the cold review's prototype: stage B first (the dynamic
witness is correct at base and stage A alone breaks it by turning main's
callsite into the 127 shape), then stage A. A and B compose by the keying
rule (anonymous literals only ever occupy Ignore slots of non-consuming
bodies and never reach a predicate), not by a projection guard.

REJECTED (measured): consumer collapse (fz-6gb's "stop specializing");
capture-read runtime axis (rebuilds the word); generalization at minting
(refuted by prototype in 125); diagnostic backstop (refuses 5 fixtures);
overlap admission (unsound for union-typed captures -- fz-kdt.167 /
the containment fixture).

RESIDUE, each owned: fz-kdt.169 (different-lambda capture-tuple splits
at forwarders: 7 corpus programs gain executables; grain question),
fz-kdt.166 (interp boxes 32 direct-layout callables with a bare fn id),
fz-kdt.168 (symmetric erasing_overlap makes exact specializations dead;
a_mixed is the live instance), fz-kdt.170 (map-typed capture at two
value types: wrong at base and head), fz-kdt.172, .173, .174, and the
proportional-compilation bycatch fz-kdt.162 (dead capture x arg product
at erased forwarders), .163 (identity-specialized duplicate bodies),
.164 (interp Int-under-F64 lenience), .165 (syntactic consumption).
Folded and closed: fz-kdt.167, fz-kdt.171. fz-kdt.157's refusing half
has a reachable witness; fz-kdt.123's no-question population is 0.

comments.text:
MEASURED by the fz-kdt.125 build (2026-09-01, base bd03d922e). Two premises in
this ticket's body and in fz-kdt.125's spec item 6 are REFUTED:

(1) "13/13 in-corpus groups are identity-separable" is an artifact of the
census helper. Its separability test regexes EVERY closure/fnref name out of a
key, including the ones sitting in CAPTURES -- and a capture is not identity.
Re-measured against the landed axis: the no-question population falls 13 -> 6,
not 13 -> 0. The 6 survivors are THIS ticket's shape exactly, same fn id and
different captures:

  00231_joined_fn_refs_enum_reduce      1  closure[Enum.reduce/3#lambda](fnref[add_a/2])
                                           vs (fnref[add_b/2])
  00277_enum_tier0_fixture              2  same lambda over two different inner closures
  00281_opaque_reducer_closure          1  as 00231
  behavior/opaque_fn_value_join         1  as 00231
  behavior/repr_seam_enum_count_after_reduce2  1  as 00277

(2) "Corpus fallout of the backstop measured ZERO" therefore does not hold. An
unrepresentable-plan DIAGNOSTIC on inseparable groups would refuse to compile
five corpus fixtures. The fz-kdt.125 build did NOT land it for that reason --
the routing half of this ticket is still open and still unbuilt, and it needs
either capture discrimination or a corpus that stops relying on the shape.

WHAT DID LAND, and it is this ticket's ABI half: `Prim::ClosureCapture` reads a
capture back out of a closure through the boundary that WROTE it, and refuses
at compile time when one callable was minted at several capture layouts that
disagree about a slot -- which is samelambda3's shape. That turns "native
executable lowering failed for index 11" into a named invariant failure. The
compile failure itself (interp: "omitted callee value 0 but target 17 needs
semantic inputs") is untouched and still this ticket's.

NOT A LIVE WRONG ANSWER, measured: 00281 with its twin function changed from
`acc + x` to `acc - x` answers -6 on interp and JIT at head. The six groups'
arm-0-takes-all is order-decided but the members are interchangeable on the
probes tried; that is luck, not a proof.

fz-kdt.119 review sequencing (2026-09-01): 119(3)'s recursive identity-preserving erasure ENLARGES this ticket's population ({:tag,#66(int)} vs {:tag,#66(float)} collapse to one question at depth -- same-fn-id/different-capture, one tuple deep). Also this ticket's compile-failure half now has a depth-1 instance with its own ticket (fz-kdt.137) which blocks 119's REFNEST-style acceptance. The backstop-policy decision this ticket owns grows correspondingly.

title: One lambda at two capture types: static cases answered by the key (brand-only forwarder erasure), dynamic cases by the word (the callable axis names the construction) -- DONE
